scams.name: Petition/Deaf Charity Clipboard Scam
scams.description: Teams of scammers approach tourists with clipboards asking if they speak English, requesting signatures for a fake 'deaf charity' petition. While distracted reading or signing, accomplices pickpocket your bags or pockets. After signing, they demand a donation. The petition is always in English (a red flag in France) and they use exaggerated sign language.
scams.avoidance: Never stop for clipboard petitioners. Say 'Non' firmly and keep walking. Never sign anything on the street. Keep hands on belongings when approached.
scams.location: Strasbourg Cathedral, Cathedral Square, Place Kléber, Petite France, Train Station

scams.name: Friendship Bracelet/String Scam
scams.description: A vendor grabs your hand and wraps colorful string around your wrist before you can refuse. Within seconds, they've tied a difficult-to-remove bracelet and demand €10-20. They become aggressive if you refuse, and may follow you. Sometimes an accomplice uses the distraction to pickpocket you.
scams.avoidance: Keep hands in pockets in tourist areas. Say 'Non' firmly and keep walking. Pull hand away immediately if they try to grab it. Carry small scissors to cut yourself free if necessary.
scams.location: Cathedral steps, Petite France, tourist walkways, Christmas markets

scams.name: Gold Ring Scam
scams.description: A stranger bends down near you and 'finds' a gold ring, asking if you dropped it. When you say no, they claim it's marked '18K gold' and must be valuable, offering to sell it. The ring is worthless brass. While engaging you, an accomplice may pickpocket you.
scams.avoidance: Simply say 'non' and walk away. Don't engage in conversation. Be aware of accomplices nearby. Keep hands on belongings.
scams.location: Near bridges, pedestrian areas, tourist walkways, Pont du Corbeau

scams.name: Tram/Public Transport Pickpocketing
scams.description: Pickpockets work crowded Strasbourg trams, especially Lines B and C serving tourist areas. They operate during rush hours and at boarding/exiting when movement is chaotic. Teams use distraction—one blocks your path while an accomplice steals from your bag. They often exit quickly as doors close.
scams.avoidance: Keep bags in front with hands on them. Don't keep valuables in back pockets. Be extra vigilant when boarding and exiting. If bumped, immediately check belongings.
scams.location: Tram Lines B and C, Gare Centrale, crowded tram stops, Cathedral area tram stops

scams.name: Counterfeit Attraction Tickets
scams.description: Unlicensed sellers approach tourists outside attractions offering 'discounted' tickets for boat tours, cathedral tower climbs, or other experiences. The tickets are fake, already used, or for non-existent tours. The seller disappears before you discover the scam. Some pose as official guides offering 'special access.'
scams.avoidance: Buy tickets only from official ticket offices. Book tours through established companies. Be suspicious of 'special deals' from strangers. Research official prices beforehand.
scams.location: Near Strasbourg Cathedral, boat tour departure points, outside tourist attractions

scams.name: Christmas Market Pickpocketing
scams.description: Strasbourg's famous Christmas markets attract over 2 million visitors, creating ideal conditions for pickpockets. Dense crowds, distracting lights, and hands occupied with food make tourists easy targets. Professional teams work the markets using distraction techniques or taking advantage of chaos.
scams.avoidance: Wear cross-body bags in front. Keep zippers secured and hands on bags. Leave valuables at hotel. Be extra vigilant in crowded market lanes. Visit during less crowded morning hours.
scams.location: Christkindelsmärik, Place Broglie, Place Kléber, all Christmas market locations

scams.name: Taxi Meter Manipulation
scams.description: Some drivers target tourists unfamiliar with local fares. They may claim the meter is broken and quote inflated prices, take unnecessarily long routes, or select higher night/weekend tariff during regular hours. Airport to city center should be approximately €40-50 during the day.
scams.avoidance: Insist on using the meter. Know approximate fares in advance. Use GPS to follow route. Consider Uber or official taxi apps. Get receipt for disputes.
scams.location: Strasbourg Airport, Gare Centrale, hotel pickups at night

scams.name: Fake Police/Document Check Scam
scams.description: Criminals pose as plainclothes police, quickly flashing fake badges. They claim to check your wallet for counterfeit currency or verify identity due to 'border security.' While examining your wallet, they steal cash. Being near the German border, they may claim special authority for 'cross-border checks.'
scams.avoidance: Ask to see official ID clearly and note badge number. Insist on going to nearest police station before showing documents. Never hand over wallet to anyone on street. Call 17 if suspicious.
scams.location: Tourist areas, near borders, tram stops, quiet streets at night

scams.name: Restaurant Menu Overcharging
scams.description: Tourist restaurants near major attractions use tactics to overcharge. Different menus in different languages show different prices. Waiters bring expensive bottled water without asking, add items not ordered, or charge premium prices for Alsatian specialties. Some insist on automatic gratuity despite service being included.
scams.avoidance: Ask for French menu and compare prices. Request 'une carafe d'eau' (tap water) - it's free. Check bill carefully. Know service is included in French prices. Walk a few streets from monuments for better value.
scams.location: Cathedral Square restaurants, Petite France terraces, tourist-heavy areas

scams.name: ATM Skimming
scams.description: Criminals attach skimming devices to ATMs capturing card data and PINs. Private ATMs like Euronet charge excessive fees and poor exchange rates. Some offer Dynamic Currency Conversion at terrible rates. Card trap devices may also be used - your card gets stuck and a 'helpful' stranger watches you enter PIN.
scams.avoidance: Use ATMs inside bank branches only. Cover keypad when entering PIN. Wiggle card slot before inserting. Decline dynamic currency conversion. If card gets stuck, don't leave - call bank.
scams.location: Standalone ATMs, tourist area ATMs, private ATMs (Euronet, Travelex)

scams.name: Bump and Grab/Distraction Theft
scams.description: A well-dressed person 'accidentally' bumps into you, spills something on you, or drops items near your feet. While apologizing and helping, an accomplice steals from your bag. Another variation: someone points out a 'stain' on your back to distract you.
scams.avoidance: If spilled on, immediately check belongings and move away. Don't let strangers touch your clothing. Be suspicious of any unusual contact. Keep bags secured in front.
scams.location: Crowded tourist areas, Cathedral entrances, tram stops, markets

scams.name: Street Vendor Overcharging
scams.description: Unlicensed vendors sell cheap souvenirs or photos at inflated prices. They target tourists at photo spots, offering to take pictures then demanding payment. Some sell 'authentic Alsatian' items that are mass-produced imports. They become aggressive if you refuse or negotiate.
scams.avoidance: Buy souvenirs from established shops. Decline offers from street vendors. Never hand camera/phone to unsolicited helpers. Most legitimate vendors have fixed prices displayed.
scams.location: Near Cathedral, tourist photo spots, Petite France bridges
